topics.label: Introduction to the lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with introductory remarks comparing complement to other complex biological pathways.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the complement system's general architecture, naming conventions, and the central role of C3 cleavage.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that drive C3 convertase formation and trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions of complement, including opsonization, inflammation, and direct cell lysis.

topics.label: Regulation and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the varied disease manifestations and clinical risks associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary mechanisms pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
